{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZcuFgg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDD8VY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 43, "title": "Correct Z80 stack and EX (SP) memory-access ordering", "body": "## Problem

`crates/msx-core/src/cpu.rs:163` implements PUSH through the low-byte-first `write16` helper. CALL, RST and interrupt entry share this path. `EX (SP),HL/IX/IY` also uses that helper at line 577. These operations require high-byte-first writes; ordinary word stores must retain their existing order.

Final RAM contents can conceal the defect. On MSX2, an access to FFFFh can change expanded-slot selection before the adjacent access, so reversing writes can route data to the wrong mapped device. This affects shared CPU behavior across firmware, cartridge and disk execution. No specific commercial-game failure has been observed.

## Expected outcome

Stack-producing operations write the high byte at original SP−1 before the low byte at original SP−2, with 16-bit wrapping. EX reads the low byte at SP and high byte at SP+1 before writing the original register’s high byte at SP+1 and low byte at SP. Existing architectural results, flags and elapsed timing remain correct.

## Context

- Evaluation baseline: clean local HEAD and inspected GitHub main both equal `0ea455fc9dabd42be6e7abeafe2c8305f844b8b2`. Relevant files are `crates/msx-core/src/cpu.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `tests/cpu.rs`, `tests/ram_mapper.rs`, `tests/fetch_timing.rs` and `docs/architecture.md`.
- [Zilog UM0080](https://www.zilog.com/docs/z80/um0080.pdf), printed pages 115–118, explicitly documents PUSH sequencing. Pages 127–129 describe EX results but do not explicitly establish its write sequence.
- [Pinned openMSX CPU implementation](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/cpu/CPUCore.cc) corroborates stack and EX ordering through `PUSH`, `ex_xsp_SS` and `WR_WORD_rev_slow`. Use it as behavioral evidence; independently author implementation and tests.
- Concrete inferred reproduction: select expanded RAM in page 3, set SP=0000h and PUSH a value whose high byte hides that RAM. Hardware writes FFFFh first, so the subsequent FFFEh write must respect the changed mapping. Current code writes FFFEh first.
- Open Issues/PRs are empty; stack/order searches found no dedicated task. Earlier #33/#34 corrected fetch waits. [Existing CI](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/actions/runs/39995232059) reports 156 Rust and 98 browser tests passing, including existing CPU stack/interrupt tests. Those tests inspect results without recording memory-access order. No builds or application tests were run during this investigation.
- Scope: correct these CPU access sequences, add focused regressions and update relevant accuracy documentation. Access-phase synchronization, contention and unrelated undocumented flags remain separate gaps.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement correct ordering for PUSH BC/DE/HL/AF/IX/IY, unconditional and taken conditional CALL, RST, NMI and supported IM0/IM1/IM2 stack entry. Untaken CALL performs no stack access. Let each byte access pass through the current bus mapping without instruction-specific hardware bypasses.
- [ ] Correct EX (SP),HL/IX/IY, preserving both reads before either write, unchanged SP and flags, and the captured exchange value.
- [ ] Add independently calculated access-recording Bus tests asserting addresses, values and sequence, alongside final state. Cover the listed instruction paths, conditional outcomes, SP wrapping at 0000h/0001h for pushes, and SP=FFFFh for exchanges. Keep opcode/operand fetches distinguishable from stack accesses.
- [ ] Add CPU-executed MSX2 integration probes using the existing FFFFh expanded-slot register. Demonstrate RAM becoming hidden and becoming visible between PUSH byte writes; also cover EX at SP=FFFEh. Assert selector state and underlying RAM retention/change. Add an MSX1 flat-RAM control. At least one ordering regression must demonstrably fail against the baseline and pass after correction; record the Coordinator’s actual results.
- [ ] Guard ordinary `LD (nn),HL/IX/IY` and ED word stores against reversal, including address wrapping. Preserve POP/RET low-byte-first reads. Check returned cycles and `tstates` increments under both standalone and MSX fetch policies; retain existing interrupt, refresh, EI/HALT and device-timing behavior.
- [ ] Preserve MSX1/MSX2 slots, video, PSG/SCC audio, disk safety, SRAM/persistence, firmware selection, Wasm/browser behavior and ownership/provenance. Use original fixtures and existing lawful assets. Document ordered accesses and remaining timing approximations.
- [ ] Coordinator completes README checks before merge: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, and `npm test`, with documented dependency/browser setup as needed. Review the complete diff and evidence against this Issue, resolve blocking findings, and accurately report failures, skipped and unperformed checks.

## Optional validation

Compare an original access trace with a pinned reference emulator before merge if available. This was not performed here. Physical hardware, proprietary firmware and commercial gameplay are unnecessary acceptance prerequisites; passing these regressions does not establish broad commercial compatibility.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
